dailyWageTax.title: Daily Worker Tax Calculator
dailyWageTax.subtitle: Enter a daily wage to see the withholding income tax, local income tax, employment insurance and take-home pay for daily (day-labor) earned income. No income tax up to ₩150,000 a day, and none up to ₩187,000 when paid daily (small-amount exemption).

u.wageHint: Total paid per day, including non-taxable meal allowance. Up to ₩150,000 is covered by the earned income deduction.
u.daysHint: Days worked for the same employer in a month (1–31). After 3+ months of continuous employment with the same employer you count as a regular employee.

mode.label: Payment schedule
mode.hint_day: Paid one day at a time: tax under ₩1,000 per payment is not collected (small-amount exemption).
mode.hint_week: Paid a week at a time: the daily taxes of that week are added up before the ₩1,000 test.
mode.hint_month: Paid the whole month at once: all daily taxes are added up before the ₩1,000 test.

u.mealHint: Meal allowance is tax-free up to ₩200,000 a month when meals are not provided. For this many days, up to {max} KRW a day is applied.
u.eiHint: Daily workers are covered regardless of hours. Turn off if you were newly hired at age 65 or older (no employee share).

result.label: Take-home pay for {days} days
result.sub: {wage} KRW × {days} days = {gross} KRW, minus {ded} KRW in taxes and insurance

table.caption: Daily worker tax and insurance breakdown

u.formula: Daily income tax = ({taxable} − 150,000) × 6% × (1 − 55%) = {tax} KRW, local income tax {local} KRW
u.formulaNone: Taxable daily pay is ₩150,000 or less, so the ₩150,000 daily deduction leaves no income tax.

small.exempt: Tax per payment is under ₩1,000, so it is not collected. {amount} KRW was exempted this period (Income Tax Act Art. 86).
small.lump: If the same {days} days were paid at once, the daily taxes would be added up and {tax} KRW income tax plus {local} KRW local tax would be withheld.
small.daily: If paid daily, the {tax} KRW daily tax would be under ₩1,000 and not collected. Lump-sum payments are judged on the summed daily tax.

u.separate: Daily earned income is taxed separately and final at withholding, so it is not included in year-end settlement or the May income tax return.

share.headline: {wage} KRW/day → {net} KRW take-home
share.text: A daily wage of {wage} KRW leaves {net} KRW a day, {total} KRW for {days} days

cmp.title: What if 3.3% (business income) were withheld?
cmp.desc: Compares the same {gross} KRW treated as freelancer business income with 3.3% withholding.
points: Daily earned income deducts ₩150,000 a day, applies 6% and a 55% tax credit, so the real rate is 2.7% of the excess over ₩150,000 (2.97% with local tax).
3.3% is withheld from freelance business income (lecturers, contractors) earned without an employment relationship: 3% income tax + 0.3% local tax.
3.3% is a prepayment settled in the May comprehensive income tax return (refund or extra payment); daily earned income tax is final at withholding.

Note: if you worked under the employer's direction at set times and places for a daily wage, you are likely a daily worker. Being paid as 3.3% may leave no employment insurance record for unemployment benefits.

ins.title: When are social insurances deducted?

items.name: Employment
items.rule: Applies to daily workers even with short hours. Employee 0.9%; none if newly hired at 65+. From Jan 1, 2027 coverage switches from working hours to earnings (note: threshold set by decree).

items.name: Pension
items.rule: Workplace member if employed 1+ month and working 8+ days or 60+ hours a month, or earning ₩2.2M+ a month (employee 4.75%). Construction: 8+ days or ₩2.2M+ (from Jul 1, 2025).

items.name: Health
items.rule: Daily workers employed under 1 month are excluded. Employed 1+ month and working 8+ days a month makes you an employee member (3.595% + long-term care) (note).

ins.estimate: If you have worked 1+ month and 8+ days this month, about {pension} KRW pension, {health} KRW health and {care} KRW long-term care ({total} KRW total) may also be deducted (2026 rates, note). Not included above.
ins.under8: With fewer than 8 workdays this month you are usually not covered by pension or health insurance, though 60+ hours or ₩2.2M+ monthly earnings can trigger pension coverage.

u.disclaimer: Estimates based on the Income Tax Act and Local Tax Act as of October 2026 and 2026 insurance rates. Rounding and employer practice may cause small differences.

formula.title: The formula
items: Daily income tax = (wage − non-taxable − ₩150,000) × 6% × 45% = 2.7% of the excess over ₩150,000
Daily deduction ₩150,000 (Income Tax Act Art. 47②), withholding rate 6% (Art. 129①4), tax credit 55% (Art. 59③)
Local income tax is 10% of income tax, so the total is 2.97% of the excess over ₩150,000.

smallTax.title: Small-amount exemption and ₩187,000
items: Withholding tax under ₩1,000 is not collected (Income Tax Act Art. 86).
At ₩187,000/day the daily tax is ₩999, so daily payment means ₩0; from ₩187,038 it reaches ₩1,000.
When several days are paid at once, the summed daily tax is tested (NTS ruling 법인46013-343). ₩187,000 × 20 days paid at month-end means ₩19,980 withheld.
No income tax means no local income tax either.

vs33.title: Daily 6% vs. 3.3%
items: Daily earned income: wages from an employer, withheld at 6% × 45% and taxed separately (final).
Business income 3.3%: freelance income without employment, settled in the next May's income tax return.
3.3% withheld may be partly refunded after expenses and deductions in the May return. Try the freelancer tax calculator.

worker.title: Who is a daily worker?
items: Someone paid by the day or hour and not continuously employed by the same employer for 3+ months (Income Tax Act Enforcement Decree Art. 20).
On construction sites the limit is 1 year with the same employer (note: other exceptions such as stevedoring in the decree).
After 3+ months of continuous employment you are taxed as a regular employee via the withholding table and year-end settlement (note).
Daily earned income is not part of year-end settlement or the May return, but counts as income for the earned income tax credit (note).

employer.title: Employer duties
items: Withhold income and local tax at payment and file/pay by the 10th of the following month (semiannual if approved).
Submit the daily earned income payment statement monthly by the last day of the following month (Income Tax Act Art. 164①).
File the employment/industrial accident insurance work report by the 15th of the following month; including the tax fields counts as the payment statement (note).
Late or missing statements incur a penalty (note: 0.25% of the amount paid, 0.125% if filed within 1 month of the deadline).
